title: Represent and Describe Data in a Box Plot
focus: Read and represent data using box plots

items.stem: What information does the box in a box plot represent?
choices: The range between the smallest and largest values
The interquartile range, which contains the middle 50% of the data
The average of all the data values
The difference between the median and the maximum value

items.stem: A box plot shows the following five-number summary for test scores: minimum = 45, Q1 = 60, median = 75, Q3 = 85, maximum = 95. Which statement correctly describes this data? Show or explain your work.
choices: Half of the students scored between 60 and 85.
The median score is closer to the maximum than the minimum.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about box plots are true? (Select ALL that apply.)
choices: The median divides the data set into two equal parts.
The length of the box shows the interquartile range (IQR).
Whiskers always extend to the minimum and maximum data values without exception.
Outliers can sometimes appear as points outside the whiskers in a box plot.

items.stem: A box plot shows the distribution of the number of books read by students in one month: minimum = 2, Q1 = 5, median = 8, Q3 = 10, maximum = 15. Explain what this box plot tells you about how many books most students read and describe the spread of the data. Show or explain your work.
